messages:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a steady cross-region spill of inference traffic for the last 3 hours, pushing cost up and saturating the EU pool. Not a full outage but latency tail creeping. We need a short-term routing strategy that both reduces cost and prevents queue growth.

liam: Do we have a breakdown of where the spill is coming from? is it specific routes/models or general overflow?

maya: Mostly high-RTT generative routes (chat) on model rdx-large v2. Traffic starts local, then a chunk gets routed to eu-west1 and then to us-east when eu is saturated. Costs up ~28% compared to baseline.

capacity-bot: Automated alert: eu-west1 GPU util 92% (sustained 12m), queue depth avg 38, incoming rate +18% vs hour-ago. Estimated spill ratio 0.22.

liam: Ok. Short term I propose a "gradient" routing policy: prefer local, then near-region, then fall back to cheaper quantized model variant in the same region before going cross-zone. This keeps traffic inside region unless capacity is unavailable and favors model fallback over long hops.

andrew: Agree on prioritizing model fallback. Cross-region hops add egress and latency. How do you want to enforce admission control? token buckets per-region?

liam: Yeah — per-region dynamic token buckets tied to available GPU slots. Simple rule: if local tokens < 10% of max, route to fallback-model-local (quantized) rather than cross-region. If fallback saturates, allow small spill window to near-region.

maya: Example config we could roll behind feature flag: 
```yaml
routing_policy: gradient-backpressure
buckets:
  - name: local
    capacity_share: 0.8
  - name: fallback-local
    model_preference: rdx-large-v2-quant
    capacity_share: 0.12
  - name: near-region
    max_spill_pct: 0.06
    regions: [eu-central1, eu-west3]
```

sophia: Two ops notes: 1) expose the bucket fill-levels in Console per-route so SREs can see when routing kicks in, 2) add a tracing tag so we can measure p90/p99 after fallback vs cross-region.

andrew: Also need to surface cost delta per route so product teams know ROI of fallback vs spill. If fallback reduces quality we may need to gate by QoS metric.

ops-oncall: Rolling this without throttles could cause oscillation — can we add a cooldown window for switching to cross-region? e.g., only allow cross-region spill if local queue > threshold for 3 consecutive minutes.

liam: Yep, implement cooldown + hysteresis. Also suggest a conservative rollout: start with 1% of traffic to new policy, then 5, 20, 100 with canary metrics around latency and cost.

maya: I'll draft the RFC (short) with config, telemetry, and rollout plan. Action items: 
- maya: RFC + feature-flag PR by EOD tomorrow
- liam: implement bucket logic + cooldown (pi branch)
- sophia: Console panels for bucket metrics + trace tag
- andrew: cost-per-route delta metric and QoS flag
- ops-oncall: prepare rollback playbook and alert thresholds

liam: One more: for long tail prevention we should ensure KV cache warmup on fallback-models so prefix caching reduces token compute. Add to RFC.

ops-oncall: +1 — also watch network retries; if retries spike, immediate rollback.

maya: Thanks — will ping when RFC is up. :pray:
